title: Gilboa fossil forest
summary: Near Gilboa in Schoharie County, New York, Devonian tree fossils from about 380 million years ago were first noted in the Schoharie Creek in 1850 by an amateur naturalist. A 2007 Nature paper described the Gilboa stumps, an intact Wattieza crown attached to an Eospermatopteris trunk, and reconstructed a tree-fern-like plant at least 8 m tall.

uncertainty.note: "380 million years ago" (Gilboa Fossils museum). Years are Ma with no 1950 offset.

as_recorded.value: 380 million years ago, during the Devonian Period

where.modern_name: Gilboa, Schoharie County, New York, USA
where.historical_name: Gilboa area on the Schoharie Creek, Devonian; no polities

importance.justification: Described as the Earth's earliest forest stumps, a key record of early trees.
